deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is not Riemann's own sheet. It is an editor's copy (Weber/Dedekind-style headings 'Zu Seite 12. Auf einem Blatt findet sich:' and '(Entwurf eines Briefes)') of two items belonging to Riemann's 1861 Paris prize essay on heat conduction, the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae'. The previous page is the Latin classification of the cases m=1..4. The next page copies the Comptes rendus prize announcements.

PART A: French note to p.12 of the Commentatio.
Notation (modern): s = (s_1..s_n) are coordinates. β_{ιι'} = g_ij(s) is a symmetric matrix, here the quadratic form arising from the conductivity transformation. d, δ, δ' are independent first-order variations, all assumed to commute with one another; this assumption is mine but standard. Write ∂_k for ∂/∂s_k.

Condition 2. δ'(g_ij ds^i ds^j) − 2d(g_ij ds^i δ's^j) = 0 for all δ'.
- Expand, using δ'd = dδ'.
- The g·ds·dδ's terms cancel.
- The remainder is δ's^j [∂_j g_ik ds^i ds^k − 2∂_k g_ij ds^i ds^k − 2g_ij d²s^i].
- Since this vanishes for all δ's: g_jl d²s^l = −Γ_{j,ik} ds^i ds^k, where Γ_{j,ik} = ½(∂_i g_jk + ∂_k g_ji − ∂_j g_ik).
- Equivalently d²s^l = −Γ^l_{ik} ds^i ds^k. This is the geodesic (parallel-transport) choice of second differentials.

Condition 3 gives in the same way δ²s^l = −Γ^l_{ik} δs^i δs^k.

Condition 1. δ'(g ds δs) − δ(g ds δ's) − d(g δs δ's) = 0.
- Expand with all mixed variations commuting.
- The terms g·δ'ds·δs and g·δs·dδ's cancel, as do g·ds·δ'δs and g·ds·δδ's.
- The remainder is δ's^j[∂_k g_il ds^i δs^l ... ] − 2 g_ij dδs^i δ's^j = 0.
- Hence dδs^l = −Γ^l_{ik} ds^i δs^k.

The expression to be formed is E = δδ(g_ij ds^i ds^j) − 2dδ(g_ij ds^i δs^j) + dd(g_ij δs^i δs^j).
- With commuting variations, the third-order variations cancel: 2g ds δδds − 2g ds dδδs − 2g δs ddδs + 2g δs ddδs = 0.
- What remains is a quadrilinear form in ds, δs.
- Because Γ=0 at the point, it is easiest to evaluate in Riemann normal coordinates (my step), where g_ij = δ_ij − (1/3)R_ikjl x^k x^l and second variations vanish:
  - term 1 = −(2/3) R(d,δ,d,δ);
  - term 2 = −2·(1/3) R(d,δ,d,δ);
  - term 3 = −(2/3) R(d,δ,d,δ).
- So E = −2 R_ikjl ds^i δs^k ds^j δs^l.
- Equivalently E = Σ (ιι',ι''ι''') p_{ιι'} p_{ι''ι'''} with p_{ιι'} = ds_ι δs_ι' − ds_ι' δs_ι. This is the Riemann curvature quadrilinear form of the Commentatio.
- In 2D it equals −2K (g(d,d)g(δ,δ) − g(d,δ)²), K the Gaussian curvature (sign per the convention above).

Purpose. Vanishing of this form for all ds, δs is Riemann's criterion that Σβ ds ds can be transformed into a constant-coefficient form, i.e. flatness. That is the integrability question in the prize problem: when can the conduction equation be reduced to the isotropic one.

PART B: draft letter (French) to Élie de Beaumont, secrétaire perpétuel of the Académie des sciences.
- Riemann says he submitted a few days earlier, via the Secrétariat, a memoir on the prize question with the epigraph 'Et his principiis via ad majora sternitur'.
- He asks that it be admitted to the competition and believes the question is solved.
- He admits that for lack of time the calculations are not given in detail, so it would need rewriting before printing.
- He explains it is written in Latin because he does not command French well enough.
- He is unsure whether it arrived in time (the deadline was 1 July 1861).
- If it is not admitted, he asks for its return to Mr. Siggelkow, Districtsactuar, Schwerin, Mecklenburg.
- The next page's Comptes rendus excerpts show the memoir (No. 2) was received and later judged incomplete ('s'est borné à esquisser une méthode').
errors: The derivation relies implicitly on all first-order variations d, δ, δ' commuting (dδ' = δ'd, etc.). The cancellation of third-order variations in E also requires dδδ = δδd and ddδ = δdd. Riemann does not state this assumption on this sheet.

The transcription's 'δ'δ''' at the start of the expression is almost certainly a misreading of 'δδ' (= δ²). The text itself speaks of the second-order variations d², dδ, δ², and only that reading gives the symmetric curvature expression.

results.what: Choice of second variations d²s, dδs, δ²s via the three conditions holding for all δ'; this is equivalent to d²s^l = −Γ^l_{ik} ds^i ds^k etc., with Christoffel symbols of the form Σβ ds ds.
results.modern_name: Christoffel symbols / geodesic (normal-coordinate) second differentials, Levi-Civita connection

results.what: The expression δδΣβdsds − 2dδΣβdsδs + ddΣβδsδs as a quadrilinear form in (ds, δs) whose vanishing characterizes flatness.
results.modern_name: Riemann curvature tensor / sectional curvature (Riemann's 'Commentatio' 1861 formulation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Habilitationsvortrag 1854, Paris Commentatio 1861, published 1876 in Werke)

results.what: Draft cover letter to Élie de Beaumont accompanying the Latin prize memoir with the epigraph 'Et his principiis via ad majora sternitur'.
results.modern_name: Historical documentation of the 1861 Paris prize submission

deep.surprise_reason: Both items are well-documented parts of Riemann's 1861 Paris Commentatio, published in the Werke (1876), with the curvature expression and the epigraph widely known. This is an editorial copy of a supplementary sheet and the cover-letter draft. It is a nice confirmation of how the second variations were fixed, but nothing is new.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y'); G=Function('G')(x); g=Matrix([[1,0],[0,G]]); X=[x,y]; Gam=[[[sum(g.inv()[l,m]*(diff(g[m,i],X[k])+diff(g[m,k],X[i])-diff(g[i,k],X[m]))/2 for m in range(2)) for k in range(2)] for i in range(2)] for l in range(2)]
checkable.asserts: Setup: Christoffel symbols of the 2D metric diag(1,G(x)). These are the solutions d2s^l=-Gam[l][i][k]*ds^i*ds^k of the three conditions on the page.

checkable.sympy: R = lambda a,b,c,e: sum(g[a,m]*(diff(Gam[m][b][e],X[c])-diff(Gam[m][b][c],X[e])+sum(Gam[m][c][n]*Gam[n][b][e]-Gam[m][e][n]*Gam[n][b][c] for n in range(2))) for m in range(2)); simplify(R(0,1,0,1) + sqrt(G)*diff(sqrt(G),x,2)) == 0
checkable.asserts: The curvature component equals -sqrt(G)*(sqrt(G))'', i.e. K*det g with K=-(sqrt G)''/sqrt G (up to sign convention). This is the Gaussian curvature that E is proportional to.

checkable.sympy: R=Function('R'); # normal coords: g_ij = delta_ij - (1/3) R_ikjl x^k x^l ; E = sum(d2g[i,j](delta,delta)*d[i]*d[j]) - 2*sum(d2g[i,j](d,delta)*d[i]*delta[j]) + sum(d2g[i,j](d,d)*delta[i]*delta[j])
checkable.asserts: In Riemann normal coordinates the page's expression E equals -2*R_ikjl d^i delta^k d^j delta^l. In 2D with constant curvature K this is -2*K*(g(d,d)*g(delta,delta)-g(d,delta)**2).

checkable.sympy: s1,s2,a,b=symbols('s1 s2 a b'); g=Matrix([[1,0],[0,s1**2]]); # polar coords of the plane, K=0: compute E with d2s=-Gamma ds ds etc. and check simplify(E)==0
checkable.asserts: For a flat metric written in curvilinear coordinates (polar), the expression E vanishes identically. This is the flatness criterion.

transcription_corrections: 'δ'δ'' Σ β ds ds' at the beginning of the expression should read 'δδ Σ β_{ι,ι'} ds_ι ds_ι'' (i.e. δ²), matching the 'variations du second ordre d², dδ, δ²'.
'j'ai du l'écrire' is in the source; read as 'j'ai dû'.

The address line: the inserted French version is 'à Schwérin' (transcribed 'Suérin', likely a misreading). The surname is uncertain between 'Siggelkow' and 'Liggelkow' in the hand; 'Siggelkow' (a Mecklenburg name) is preferable.
The title line '(Entwurf eines Briefes)' is an editorial German heading, as is 'Zu Seite 12. Auf einem Blatt findet sich:'. This page is an editor's copy, not Riemann's autograph.
